judgments.reasoning_cat1: The substance (other Borrowers must cover a defaulting Borrower's payment) is plain, though the subsection is lettered "(a)" where it should be "(c)".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.13(a)-(b) and the preamble's joint and several designation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It cross-refers to "Section 2.15," a section that does not exist, and declares the obligations enforceable "irrespective of the validity… of this Agreement," a self-referentially odd formulation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The intended reference is plainly Section 2.13, and the surrounding subsections are consistent; the mis-citation is one of several in the document.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long catalogue of waivers bracketed by two overlapping carve-outs ("Except as otherwise expressly provided in this Agreement" and "(except as otherwise provided in this Agreement)"), which leaves the scope of the waivers to be worked out against the rest of the document.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 12 requires various notices and Section 9.1's final paragraph waives presentment and demand; the carve-outs are doing real work but no squarely contradictory provision appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Straightforward representations and a continuing covenant to stay informed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to "the financial condition of other guarantors, if any," although no Guarantor is identified anywhere in the transaction — a harmless template remnant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It waives election-of-remedies defences by reference to "security for a guaranteed obligation" and Lender's "rights of subrogation and reimbursement," concepts that belong to guarantors, whereas these parties are co-obligors; the provision also ends with a colon rather than a period.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 13 makes New York law govern, yet this waiver is drafted entirely around Section 580d of the California Code of Civil Procedure — an unresolved tension about which law the waiver even operates under.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Sub-clause (B) refers to "Agent and Lenders" — neither term is defined in this bilateral agreement — and the waiver is framed around California antideficiency statutes in a document whose parties are a single Lender and two co-Borrowers.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 13's New York choice of law does not sit comfortably with a waiver expressly built on Sections 580a, 580b, 580d and 726 of the California Code of Civil Procedure, and the undefined "Agent" has no referent anywhere in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear as to beneficiaries, non-marshalling and reinstatement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 14.1, 14.2 and 16.7's revival provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Substantively clear subordination of contribution and subrogation claims; the subsection letter is garbled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 2.13(k) and the Section 2.3(b) waterfall.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite: intercompany debt subordinated and held in trust after a Default.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It applies on a mere "Default" while Section 2.13(j) applies unconditionally; the two are cumulative rather than inconsistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The chapeau makes the making of the initial extension of credit "conclusively deemed" to be satisfaction or waiver of every condition, and clause (a) requires filings in offices "in the opinion of Lender, desirable" — both are open-textured.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.3 imposes separate conditions to all extensions of credit, so the conclusive-waiver language is confined to the initial funding; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed list of six deliverables; "form and substance satisfactory to Lender" is the only soft element.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires Control Agreements and Cash Management Agreements at closing, while Sections 2.6(a)/(c) contemplate the cash management structure being built out over 60 days; a mild sequencing tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite; a standard secretary's certificate requirement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the "Board of Directors" and "Authorized Person" definitions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite and narrow.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the "Governing Documents" definition and Section 7.3(a).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The certificate must be "dated within 36 days of the Closing Date" — an unusual figure that the immediately following subsection states as 30 days, so one of the two numbers is wrong on the face of the document.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.1(f) uses 30 days for the equivalent foreign-jurisdiction certificates, which makes the discrepancy visible within the same Section.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The scope of jurisdictions is fixed by whether failure to qualify "would constitute a Material Adverse Change," importing that vague standard into a closing checklist.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 5.8(a) and the Material Adverse Change definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite by cross-reference to Section 6.8.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.8 does prescribe the required coverage and endorsements; accurate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 5.9's due authorisation representations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite, with an express Permitted Protest carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 6.7 and the Permitted Protest definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An open-ended due diligence condition entirely keyed to results "satisfactory to Lender," and it refers to "the Loewe-Adler collateral review," an extrinsic document nowhere defined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with Sections 3.1(m), (p), (r) and (s), all of which impose their own satisfaction standards; cumulative rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Satisfactory to Lender in its sole discretion" is unqualified, but the condition is narrow and mechanical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The four named individuals match the "Permitted Holders" list but not the five-name "Executive Officer" and "Validity Agreement Party" lists.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite in substance; the subsection letter is garbled and "shall have paid or shall pay" is loose but workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Lender Expenses definition and Section 2.5(c)'s charging authority.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite as a condition, though it approves documents not reproduced in the instrument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the "Borrower's Required Procedures" definition, which likewise contemplates pre-closing delivery and approval.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single objective dollar test as at a fixed date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches the Section 7.16(a) covenant floor, but the same $600,000,000 figure is what makes the Section 7.16(b) 0.9% leverage cap impossible to satisfy alongside a $50,000,000 facility.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It requires a "Landlord's Waiver and Consent," a document type not defined anywhere in the Agreement, for one named address.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The defined analogue is "Collateral Access Agreement" (used in Section 6.9), so the instrument uses two different labels for what appears to be the same instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Satisfaction is measured by counsel being "satisfied that such documentation provides Fund and Lender with appropriate rights and remedies" — a soft but bounded standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Overlaps with Section 3.1(m); consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The proviso — that the condition "may be satisfied by Fund providing to Lender such reasonable assurances as Lender may require" — largely dissolves the substantive requirement that all licences actually be held.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.3 and Schedule 5.3 represent that the listed licences are all that is required, so the proviso substitutes assurance for compliance in a way the representation does not contemplate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed list of four review items keyed to Lender's satisfaction; mechanical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 3.1(j) and Section 6.2's ongoing reporting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two specific, dated financial statements; entirely definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 5.11 and 6.3.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An eight-item document list, two of which are qualified "if available" — a qualifier that lets the condition be satisfied by non-delivery — and the whole is subject to "form and substance acceptable to Lender".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The parallel document list in Eligible Notes Receivable clause (r) has nine items and different timing rules, and Sections 3.3(e), 4.2 and 8.17 each restate the $250,000,000 requirement in slightly different terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All other documents and legal matters… shall be in form and substance satisfactory to Lender" is an unbounded catch-all placed after twenty specific conditions — the paradigm general-versus-specific problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Section 3.1 chapeau deems the making of the initial extension of credit to waive all conditions, which limits the practical bite of the catch-all.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The section is numbered "4.2" in a part of the document that runs 3.1 to 3.7, and the single condition reads "Manager shall have a hired a full time Controller"; both are mechanical errors on the face of the provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.2(c) refers to "a condition subsequent set forth in Section 3.2," a number that does not appear in the document as printed, so the cross-reference chain is broken.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional bring-down qualified by materiality with an earlier-date carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Section 5 chapeau, which uses the same formulation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single short condition; the sentence ends without punctuation but the meaning is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the "Default" and "Event of Default" definitions and Section 8.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite in scope, though "or other order of any nature" is a catch-all after three specific forms of relief.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the "Governmental Authority" definition and Section 8.6.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Six words with no measuring date — "no Material Adverse Change shall have occurred" gives no baseline from which the change is judged, and the defined term is itself vague.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5.11 supplies a baseline ("since the date of the latest financial statements submitted to Lender on or before the Closing Date") that this condition does not adopt, leaving two different tests for the same concept.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite in amount and content, cross-referring to the Section 3.1(t) document list; "otherwise reasonably acceptable to Lender" is the soft element.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.2 states the same $250,000,000 holding requirement as a covenant and Section 8.17 as a default trigger with a three-Business-Day cure — three overlapping formulations of one requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "A current Borrowing Base Certificate" leaves "current" undefined — a certificate dated when?
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit B-2 supplies no form (it says "[form to be provided by Lender]") and Section 6.2 requires the calculation on each Advance date and monthly, so the required content and vintage are fixed outside this condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed three-year term with a clear early-termination right on default; "subject to any notice and cure rights otherwise provided" is the only qualification.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The document contains a second provision printed as "3.4" (Intentionally Blank), and the "Maturity Date" definition points to "Section 3.4" — so the cross-reference is ambiguous.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The provision is printed as "3.4 Intentionally Blank" when it should be 3.5, duplicating the number of the Term section — a mechanical error visible on the face of the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The "Maturity Date" definition cross-refers to Section 3.4, which now identifies two different provisions; the table of contents lists 3.5 as the blank one, confirming the misprint.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but carefully sequenced: acceleration on termination, survival of duties and liens, and a release mechanic once everything is paid.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says liens remain until Obligations are "paid in full," while Section 1.4 defines repayment in full to exclude contingent indemnification and certain Bank Product Obligations — a definitional overlay that softens the literal words.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Repetitive but definite: 30 days' notice, full cash payment plus cash collateral and the Applicable Prepayment Premium.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Applicable Prepayment Premium is zero after the first anniversary, so the premium requirement here becomes formal only; Section 3.7(b) adds "if applicable" while this subsection does not.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The cross-reference is garbled ("Section 3.'Mfa)"), and the clause pairs a liquidated-damages recital with the qualifier "shall pay, if applicable," leaving unclear when the premium is in fact owed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Applicable Prepayment Premium is zero after year one, so the elaborate lost-profits recital has almost no field of operation — an awkward fit with the three-year term in Section 3.4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The grant is over "Borrower Collateral" but the closing sentence forbids disposition of "the Collateral," a defined term of wider reach — the provision switches terms mid-way.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Borrower Collateral" omits Real Property from its enumerated list while Section 4.4(c) contemplates perfecting liens on after-acquired owned Real Property and Permitted Dispositions clause (g) allows sales of Real Estate Owned; the instrument is not consistent about what is secured.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The endorsement legend is pre-printed in the name of R.E. Loans, LLC only although both Borrowers grant liens, and possession is required only "to the extent that Lender determines" perfection depends on it — two soft edges in one provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.16 says delivery is required only "to the extent necessary to comply with Section 4.2," while Sections 3.1(t), 3.3(e) and 8.17 each restate the $250,000,000 delivery requirement differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three enumerated post-default powers plus a trust obligation over Collections; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.6(a), 4.8 and 9.1(d)/(e).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Necessary or desirable to effectuate the transactions" is broad for an authorisation to file, but UCC practice makes it conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Filing Authorization Letter definition and Section 3.1(a).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, specific three-Business-Day obligation with a defined output document.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Borrower Collateral clause (c), Schedule 5.7(d) and Section 5.7(d).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All other documents… that Lender may request in its Permitted Discretion" is an open catch-all after an enumerated list, and the subsection then bolts on an intellectual-property registration regime that has little to do with its heading.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contemplates Liens on "any owned Real Property acquired after the Closing Date," which the Borrower Collateral definition does not enumerate; Section 4.5(a) gives Lender power to sign these documents if Borrowers refuse.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrow assignment of access rights with a post-default entry right; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 5.5 and 7.15's public-warehouse proviso, which requires that access be assigned to Lender.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An irrevocable power of attorney whose clauses (c) and (d) are not limited to a continuing Event of Default, unlike clauses (b), (e) and (f) — the differential drafting is deliberate but invites argument about pre-default powers.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.3's collection powers arise only on an Event of Default, so the unrestricted endorsement power in clause (d) is broader than the parallel collection provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad inspection and verification rights bounded by "reasonable notice" and "normal business hours"; conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.10(d), 6.1 and 6.5(c).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite as to the UCC control sections and the categories of accounts covered.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It permits Lender to direct liquidation of Deposit and Securities Accounts on a mere "Default," whereas Section 9.1 makes the remedies package available only on an Event of Default — a genuine mismatch in triggers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The opening clause ("Until such time as the Lender shall notify… of the revocation of such right after the occurrence and during the continuation of an Event of Default") is tangled, and it grants Borrowers power to take action "as the Borrowers may deem advisable" while simultaneously requiring compliance with Borrower's Required Procedures.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 9.1(e) and 9.1(o) give Lender overlapping and more sweeping servicing rights on default, and revocation must be "in accordance with the terms of the Servicing Agreement," a document not before the reader.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sequence is internally awkward: the note is returned once it "is repaid in its entirety" but the return is "to facilitate its payment," and release follows "promptly upon receipt of the final payment" — repayment is both premise and consequence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.6(a)(iii) requires payoff proceeds to be paid directly into a Cash Management Account, which is the mechanism the muddled sequencing here appears to assume.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear obligation to release and transfer against payment; "in accordance with the terms of this Agreement" is the only qualifier.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That qualifier points to Permitted Dispositions clause (e), which permits sales at not less than 80% of unpaid balance with proceeds to a Cash Management Account — a real constraint not restated here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three enumerated triggers and a defined output; workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 4.9(a)-(b) and 6.16's recording obligation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional chapeau; it makes the representations both "as of the date hereof" and "as of the Closing Date," which are the same date under the Closing Date definition — redundant but harmless.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 3.3(a)'s bring-down and Section 8.11's misrepresentation default.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Good and indefeasible title" to personal property is an unusual formulation, and the representation is absolute save for Permitted Liens.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The "Lien" definition expressly captures easements, covenants, conditions, restrictions and leases affecting Real Property, while Permitted Liens clause (k) rescues only easements, rights of way and zoning restrictions — so the representation is broader than the carve-out supports.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Nine sub-representations, several of which restate the eligibility criteria, and clause (i) adds a substantive requirement (development "located or… expected to be built") that appears nowhere else and is inherently imprecise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The "Eligible Notes Receivable" definition itself incorporates "the representations and warranties respecting Eligible Notes Receivable made in the Loan Documents," so definition and representation define each other circularly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It gives an unqualified representation that "all aspects of Borrowers' operations, comply with all applicable federal, state and local laws and regulations" — absolute, with no materiality or knowledge qualifier, unlike the first sentence of the same section.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.10 requires compliance only with laws whose breach could reasonably be expected to cause a Material Adverse Change, so the representation and the covenant apply different standards to the same subject.
